$comment: Where spec/openapi/fog-1.6.json came from. Regenerate both together; a snapshot with a stale provenance record is worse than no snapshot, because the diff it produces cannot be traced back to a server change.

source.$note: Dumped from FOGProject/fogproject working-1.6 directly; b25193faf is an ancestor of origin/working-1.6, verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. No local corrections -- there is no merged tree to dump from.

notes: Both live routes sit in the router's unauthenticated allowlist, so discovery needs no tokens.

The live document is built per request and includes classes contributed by plugin hooks. This snapshot fires no hooks, so it describes stock FOG. That is the intended baseline for generated cmdlets; plugin classes are a runtime concern, handled by reading the live document.
1.6 only. The 1.5 line has no commons/schema-expected.php, so there is no type source to generate against there.

The generic read routes take a server-side column filter. It is advertised as the shared ?filter= query parameter on list/count/names/ids for every class -- 204 operations -- and NOT on search, which builds its own where clause from matched ids and cannot honour one. The equivalent trailing path segment (/{class}/list/field=value) still works and wins when both are sent; it is deliberately not a documented path, because OpenAPI cannot mark a path parameter optional and describing it would add 204 paths to a 372-path document.

verifiedAgainstLiveServer.method: Deployed b25193faf to the maintainer's lab server (FOG 1.6.0-beta.3894, nginx 1.30.4 + PHP 8.3.33 + MariaDB, schema 356) and exercised the filter over HTTPS against real rows, with counts cross-checked directly against the database.
verifiedAgainstLiveServer.result: 11/11 checks passed. taskLog holds 56 rows of which 3 carry logHostID=154; ?filter=hostID%3D154 returns recordsFiltered 3 against recordsTotal 56 on /tasklog, /tasklog/count returns 3 and /tasklog/ids returns the three ids.
behaviourChecks: GET /tasklog?filter=hostID%3D154 -> recordsFiltered 3; two fields ANDed via ?filter=hostID%3D154%26type%3Derror -> 3; ?filter=hostID%3D999999 -> 0.
GET /tasklog/list/hostID=154 -> 3, and the segment still wins when a contradicting ?filter= is sent alongside it.
GET /tasklog?filter=nosuchfield%3D1 -> 400 naming the key; GET /user?filter=password%3Dx -> 400, credential fields refused.
GET /host/search/fos and /host/search/fos?filter=id%3D999999 return the SAME count: search builds its where clause in PHP and a request filter cannot replace it.
verifiedAgainstLiveServer.note: The offline generator was re-diffed against the previous snapshot as well: 372 paths, 517 operations and 53 schemas before and after, identical path set, no schema changed shape, and components.parameters gained exactly one entry.

changeLog.summary: The list filter is now discoverable. Nothing was added or removed -- the only difference is a shared ?filter= parameter on 204 existing operations.
detail: b25193faf "fix(api): document the list filter, and let it be sent as ?filter=" adds components.parameters.filter and attaches it to list/count/names/ids on all 51 classes.

The filter itself is not new. Route::defineRoutes() has always registered those four with a trailing [*:whereItems]? segment, and handleWhereItems() parse_str()s it, checks the keys against the class and refuses credential fields. GET /tasklog/list/hostID=154 has always worked.

What was wrong was the description: it appeared only on list, only in prose, and said "accepts field:value pairs" when parse_str wants field=value -- so the documented form answers 400. That is what #66 recorded as "no server-side column filter at all", and why Get-LastImageTime paged the whole of taskLog and filtered client-side.

search does NOT gain the parameter. It passes its matched ids down as a non-empty array, which the server refuses to let a request filter replace, so advertising one would repeat the defect being fixed.
No hand-edit beyond openapi.class.php was needed: _listParameters() feeds every generic read operation, so the document self-updates.

changeLog.summary: Two unrelated upstream narrowings: search is advertised only where it can answer, and the event tables went read-only. No schema changed shape and nothing was added.
detail: 4350d5048 'Emit the OpenAPI search route only for classes that have a name field' adds OpenAPI::_isSearchable(), gating /{class}/search/{item} on the same isset($databaseFields['name']) test unisearch() already applies.

Removed 20 search paths: filedeletequeue, groupassociation, history, hostautologout, hostscreensetting, imageassociation, inventory, ipxe, macaddressassociation, moduleassociation, multicastsessionassociation, nodefailure, powermanagement, printerassociation, snapinassociation, snapingroupassociation, snapinjob, snapintask, tasklog, usertracking.

70871455c 'fix(api): event tables answer no write verb (ADR 0020 decision 7)' adds history and tasklog to Route::$readOnlyClasses (usertracking was already there, which is why it lost only its search route).

Removed 8 write operations on those two: POST /history, PUT /history/{id}, DELETE /history/{id}, PUT /history/join and the same four for tasklog. Both /join paths disappear entirely because OpenAPI emits /{class}/join only when the class is writable.
22 paths and 28 operations removed in total. The search description also gained the sentence naming the extra fields host, storagenode and setting match on.
Neither commit needed a hand-edit to the document beyond openapi.class.php itself: _paths() generates from $validClasses and writableClasses(), so the document self-updates.

changeLog.summary: imagingLog retired upstream; taskLog carries the image name.
detail: 065b3fe3a feat(logs): retire imagingLog; taskLog carries the image name (ADR 0022) drops 'imaginglog' from Route::$validClasses.
Removed: the Imaginglog schema and its 7 paths - /imaginglog, /count, /ids, /join, /names, /search/{item}, /{id}.
Changed: Tasklog gained imageName (9 -> 10 properties). No other schema changed shape and nothing was added.
That commit did not touch openapi.class.php, correctly: _paths() generates from $validClasses, so the document self-updates.
